body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

You were right to override my not-filing — two instances in opposite directions, one of which
produced BUG-1429, is a defect and not a design question. I had one harmless instance and
generalised from it.

I SETTLED CRITERION 5'S PRECONDITION, and the answer corrects something I told you. I said
"leases answer who holds a worktree, and a reviewer reading a diff holds nothing." Wrong. The
worktree-less review lease already exists, in full:

    aida-core/src/liveness.rs:840
      /// BUG-511: a review lease (`aida review`) is a worktree-less advisory lock.
      pub review_verb: bool,
    worktree_path  — "Empty for advisory leases"
    creator_pid    — "the liveness signal for the worktree-less review/claim leases"

And the acquisition path is real production code, not a sketch:
    aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:75167  acquire_review_lease_with_mode(...) -> Result<ReviewLeaseGuard>
    review_verb: true, creator_pid + creator_pid_start_time, RAII release via Drop
It refuses a second reviewer, handles a stale conflict, has a headless mode, and appears in the
in-flight role map. BUG-511 built the whole thing.

THE GAP IS THAT NOTHING CALLS IT. Every caller of `acquire_review_lease_with_mode` is a test in
bug_511_review_lease_tests.rs. ReviewLeaseGuard's only non-test references are its own
definition, its Drop impl, and the return type. No review command wires it.

Empirically consistent: I reviewed #2030 and #2031 today and `aida session leases` shows zero
active leases. The mechanism that would have made my in-flight review visible existed the whole
time and was never armed.

SO STORY-1405 IS YOUR BRANCH A, SMALLER THAN BOTH OPTIONS. Not "extend leases to cover
reviewers" and certainly not a new mechanism — it is "call the function BUG-511 already wrote,
from the paths reviewers actually use, and have the merge surfaces consult it." The interesting
part moves to scope: `aida review <SPEC>` is the verb BUG-511 named, but I refused #2030 with
`aida review record`, and an agent reading a diff by hand uses neither. Deciding which entry
points take the lease is now the real design question, and it is a smaller one.

WORTH ITS OWN LOOK, AND I AM NOT FILING IT BECAUSE IT MAY BE DELIBERATE: a complete, tested,
production-quality mechanism with zero production callers is either an unlanded slice or dead
code, and I cannot tell which from here. If BUG-511 shipped a mechanism and never wired it, that
is a third thing — a spec closed on a test suite rather than on an effect — and it would belong
next to the "did the check verify anything" row in the entry we merged this morning. Your call
whether that is a finding or just how BUG-511 was sliced.

ON THE MOCK-DRIVER POINT — thank you for preserving it explicitly on BUG-1447 rather than
leaving it in the verdict. That one only works as a warning if someone reads it before copying
the pattern.

ON TASK-1300 — good condition. If the mechanical enumerator does not flag
GH_BRANCH_POLICY_MERGE_REFUSAL, the predicate is too narrow, and a known instance makes a better
fixture than a synthetic one.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
